samples.summary: Third verbatim copy of the image upload `FileInterceptor` options (limits + fileFilter) instead of one shared options object
samples.evidence: The `FileInterceptor('file', { limits: { fileSize: IMAGE_UPLOAD_MULTER_LIMIT_BYTES }, fileFilter: ... unsupportedFileTypeMessage(...) })` block is now byte-identical in three places: `packages/backend/src/image/image.controller.ts:102`, `packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:56`, and this new controller. The repo already went to the trouble of centralizing every *value* the block needs in `image/image.constants.ts` (with a spec, `image.constants.spec.ts`, asserting there is one wording) precisely because these routes must not drift; the options object itself was the obvious next thing to export from that module. Cost stays inside the codebase (the shared constants keep behavior aligned today), so minor — but a fourth route will copy it again.

samples.summary: Canonical constants doc comments still enumerate "two upload routes" / "four call sites" after a third upload route was added
samples.evidence: `image.constants.ts:10` ("both upload routes (`POST /images` and `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images`)"), `:20` ("The Multer `fileSize` limit both upload routes pass"), `:54` ("Four call sites produce it: the `fileFilter` on each of the two upload routes..."), and `image.constants.spec.ts:29` ("Two upload routes' `fileFilter`s") are the repo's own statement of who shares these constants. `POST /api/v1/shared/images` is now a third route / fifth call site and none of them were updated, so the module that exists to be the single source of truth about these routes now describes a set it no longer covers.

samples.summary: New public v1 endpoint `POST /api/v1/shared/images` is absent from both the REST-API design doc and the developer REST-API reference
samples.evidence: `docs/design/rest-api.md` §5.6 lists exactly the three v1 image routes (`POST`/`GET`/`DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images...`) and `packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:257-306` documents the Images section in detail — including the anonymous `?token=` read (`:303`) added by the sibling controller. The new anonymous *write* route, which is an externally reachable, unauthenticated API surface with its own auth rule (editor-role token) and its own throttle (30/min), appears in neither. `docs/design/sharing.md` was updated, which is the right canonical home for the sharing decision, but the API surface inventory the repo keeps in these two files is now incomplete.

samples.summary: Canonical image-spine table and its cross-workspace-copy conclusion ("`doc` is unaffected") are falsified by this change and were not updated
samples.evidence: `template-gallery.md:173-185` holds the repo's canonical table of the two image upload paths, mapping `doc` to `postSharedImage` → `POST /images` (bucket root, unauthenticated) and concluding "`doc` is unaffected" by the cross-workspace copy image loss. After this change a `doc` can hold workspace-scoped image URLs (inserted through an editor share link via `postShareTokenImage`), so both the table row and the conclusion are wrong. The related backend comment at `packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts:432-436` ("`doc` images are uploaded to the bucket root ... skipping it asserts 'docs never hold a workspace image'") is stale for the same reason — behavior there is fine because the rehost pass runs for `doc` anyway, so the cost is documentation drift on a decision the next reader will rely on.

samples.summary: cli.md's "Export image fetching" section documents the fetcher's rules in detail but not the new credential-attachment rule
samples.evidence: `docs/design/cli.md:1230-1305` is the canonical description of `createImageFetcher` — scheme allowlist, per-hop gating, the three ways to be the server, pinning, proxies. This change gives the fetcher a materially new and security-relevant behavior (an `Authorization: Bearer` value is now attached, only on an exact scheme+host+port match with the configured server, recomputed per hop so a redirect drops it — `packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:432-455`), plus a new `authorizationHeader` seam in `client/http-client.ts`. Neither is recorded in cli.md, so the doc now under-describes the component's trust behavior. Note the section already says "Another port on the same host is not covered" for the *gate*, while the credential rule is deliberately stricter — exactly the nuance the doc should carry.

samples.summary: Scope creep: `slides export` credential change is unrelated to the docs share-upload issue
samples.evidence: The issue this change serves is the docs share-link image upload (visitor ejected to `/login`). `docs export` needing the credential follows from it (docs can now hold workspace-scoped images). `slides export` does not: slides share-link mounts still refuse image upload outright (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:506-508` toasts "Image upload isn't available in shared editing"), and slides' workspace-scoped images predate this branch — so this hunk fixes a separate, pre-existing export gap and widens the blast radius of a security-sensitive change (sending an API key on export fetches) beyond what the issue asked for. Defensible as consistency, but it belongs in its own change with its own justification.

samples.summary: `loadFileDimensions` duplicates the existing private `loadImageDimensions(file)` in the spreadsheet image-upload module
samples.evidence: The new `loadFileDimensions` (image-insert.ts:97-127) is a near line-for-line copy of `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:76-96` — createObjectURL, onload/naturalWidth check, revokeObjectURL, same rejection shapes — and its own comment admits it ("Mirrors what `spreadsheet/image-upload.ts` already does for the other engines"). Both live in `packages/frontend/src/app`, so one could simply export the other, or it could join the shared browser-image module the repo already keeps at `packages/core/src/image/index.ts`. Two copies of the same measurement will drift (the copies already differ in revoke ordering and in the error wording: "Failed to read image" vs "Failed to load image").

samples.summary: Docs now writes to both image spines, contradicting this module's own stated rule about which spine in-document content belongs on
samples.evidence: `api/images.ts:6-20` states the rule: the workspace spine "is right for content *inside* a document", the root bucket "is right for anything a logged-out stranger must see". This change puts share-link docs inserts on the workspace spine (correct by that rule) but leaves the docs *owner* insert on the root-bucket `POST /images` (`image-insert.ts:23-25` → `docxImageUploader` → `export-utils.ts:31`). One document can therefore hold URLs from both spines with different read gating, different copy semantics, and different export requirements — which is why `shared-document.tsx` needs the "resolver matches only the workspace path" caveat and why the design doc has to explain the split. Migrating the docs owner path was out of scope for the issue, so the cost stays inside the codebase; recording it as a known follow-up in `docs/design/sharing.md` (which it partly does) is the minimum.

samples.summary: Share-link upload path does no client-side size/type check or downscale, unlike the sheets uploader
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader` posts the file straight through, so an anonymous editor dropping a 15 MB phone photo gets a 413 from Multer surfaced as a toast. The established pattern in this repo for an in-document image insert is `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:25-45`: validate MIME, downscale over the cap rather than refuse (issue #815), and only then upload. The docs owner path has the same gap today, so this is pre-existing rather than introduced — but the share-link visitor is the user least able to recover from the refusal.
